title: feat: automate Buzz v0.5.0 publication
body:
## Summary

- Upgrade the Cloudron package to Buzz `v0.5.0` as package `0.1.7`, with independently verified upstream image provenance.
- Add a guarded `main`-branch workflow that builds an amd64 GHCR package image, verifies anonymous access, generates an immutable Cloudron catalog entry with the pinned Cloudron CLI, and atomically publishes the catalog commit and package tag.
- Add rollback-focused catalog publisher tests and document the standing reviewed-merge publication contract.

## Why

The configured Cloudron instance could not auto-update beyond package `0.1.4` because later source versions were never added to the public `CloudronVersions.json` catalog. This closes that source-to-catalog automation gap while retaining explicit review, provenance, and fail-closed publication gates.

## Key decisions

- A reviewed package-version change merged to `main` is the publication authorization; the upstream monitor still cannot publish directly.
- Catalog entries use immutable `@sha256:` image references and remain append-only.
- Publication is canonical-repository-only and requires either a trusted merged PR or explicit workflow dispatch.
- Registry publication stops before catalog mutation unless the image is anonymously readable.

## Runtime Testing

`runtime-verified`: a disposable Cloudron app using package `0.1.7` / Buzz `v0.5.0` passed clean server-side build and install, readiness, supervisor status, restart, backup, restore, and post-restore readiness. The disposable app was then uninstalled and its absence verified.

## Verification

- `./test/package-test.sh`
- `./test/verify-buzz-image.sh`
- `shellcheck` on all runtime, publisher, and test shell scripts
- `actionlint .github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish.yml`
- Shell complexity, nesting, file-size, and Bash 3.2 regression gates
- `docker build --platform linux/amd64 --tag cloudron-buzz-app:test .`
- amd64 ELF and Buzz binary smoke checks
- Real Cloudron CLI catalog-generation fixture
- CodeRabbit credential-scope and fixture-isolation findings fixed in `ad9356c`
- Review evidence bundle: `943d0c110644daed89e4bc0bb07e0d07273907881c21b7330a577474268e96be` (prompt-injection scan clean)

## Release plan and remaining risk

After merge, the new workflow should publish package `0.1.7`, tag `v0.1.7`, and the matching GitHub release. Its first GHCR run fails closed if GitHub creates the package as private; catalog state is not changed until anonymous access succeeds. After publication, the configured Cloudron app will be observed through its automatic update and health/migration checks.

Tracking: Beads `buzz-268`.

title: t015: Protect Buzz catalog publication with a scoped PAT
body:
## Goal

Prepare Buzz catalog publication for reviewed, protected `main` while retaining fully automatic immutable catalog and tag publication.

## Changes

- use the per-repository `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` only in the final atomic push step
- fail closed when the credential is absent
- mark generated catalog commits `[skip ci]` to prevent PAT-triggered workflow recursion
- isolate GitHub release creation in a following step that uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`
- document least-privilege scope, rollback, and recovery
- add regression checks for credential count and operation ordering
- restore the `t015` to issue #39 task mapping after the atomic claim helper could not persist it

## Security

The configured fine-grained PAT is selected for this repository only and grants only `Contents: Read and write`. Registry authentication and release API calls continue to use `GITHUB_TOKEN`; no credential value is committed or logged.

## Verification

- `bash test/package-test.sh`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish.yml`
- `git diff --check`

## Rollout

After merge, apply classic protection to `main` with one required approval, stale-review dismissal, force-push and deletion blocking, and administrator enforcement disabled.
